_meta.purpose: Demo safety net for Scene 2.5. Used only if Track A's find-contradictions skill (A.6) produces mush at hour 8. Hand-verified from corpus reading on 2026-05-16.
_meta.verification_notes: PG himself explicitly flags this as a change of view ("I used to think of VCs as piratical"). Same topic (VC character), 3 years apart (Mar 2005 → Apr 2008), substantive flip (arrogant/devious → upstanding/timid), not a hedge or refinement. Meets every C.5.5 criterion.

claim_a.text: They were the most arrogant people I've met in my life. And I've met a lot of arrogant people. Even a VC friend of mine dislikes VCs. 'Assholes,' he says. ... It explains why they steal your ideas. Every founder knows that VCs will tell your secrets to your competitors if they end up investing in them. The only reason VCs are so sneaky is the giant deals they do. With so much at stake, they have to be devious.

claim_b.text: I used to think of VCs as piratical: bold but unscrupulous. On closer acquaintance they turn out to be more like bureaucrats. They're more upstanding than I used to think (the good ones, at least), but less bold.

contradiction_summary: In 2005 he called VCs arrogant, sneaky, devious — they'd 'steal your ideas' and meet you only to brief competitors; in 2008 he conceded VCs were actually more upstanding than he'd thought, just bureaucratic and timid — and explicitly flagged the change with 'I used to think.'
